units.title: The Cardiomyopathy Definition and Seven Types, the DCMP Presentation Table, MRI Uses and Pathophysiology
units.sec: The Cardiomyopathy Definition and Seven Types, the DCMP Presentation Table, MRI Uses and Pathophysiology
units.guide:
Cardiomyopathy is myocardial disease with a structurally/functionally abnormal heart after excluding CAD, hypertension, valvular disease and congenital disease (p331). Seven types are DCMP, HCM, RCMP, Takotsubo, arrhythmogenic RV dysplasia, LV non-compaction and tachycardia-induced disease.
DCMP systolic presentation has fatigue/palpitations, tachycardia from low CO/sympathetic overactivity, a down-and-out apex and prominent S3; diastolic presentation has dyspnea, edema/raised JVP and crepitations. Males > females.
MRI is gold standard for EF, RV function, amyloidosis/sarcoidosis and ischemia versus infarction. DCMP runs LV dilatation/thinning/systolic dysfunction → diastolic failure → LV failure → RV failure, with global hypokinesia and 25% of all heart-failure cases.

units.title: Other Heart-Failure Causes, the Genetic Table and Variable Penetrance, Etiology Branches, Complications and the Thrombus Figure
units.sec: Other Heart-Failure Causes, the Genetic Table and Variable Penetrance, Etiology Branches, Complications and the Thrombus Figure
units.guide:
Other heart-failure causes are valvular, congenital and ischemia-related (p332). Genetics accounts for 30% with a positive family history: DCMP is autosomal dominant (TV titin > myosin heavy chain 7 > troponin I), ARVD autosomal recessive (desmosome) and LV non-compaction X-linked recessive (tafazzin), with variable penetrance/expression.
Peripartum and alcohol-induced CMP have good prognoses; drug-induced CMP is bad. Toxin/nutrition deficiencies are thiamine, selenium (sub-Himalayan Keshan disease) and carnitine; autoimmune sarcoidosis/hemochromatosis have a dilated > restrictive component; endocrine causes are pheochromocytoma, thyroid disease and obesity; inflammatory CMP is myocarditis.
Complications are thromboembolism, arrhythmias from a dilated LV, sudden cardiac death and decompensation with increased mortality; the figure shows a DCMP intraventricular thrombus on POCUS ECHO.

units.title: DCMP Investigations, Transplant, Angina with Normal Coronaries, and Peripartum Cardiomyopathy
units.sec: DCMP Investigations, Transplant, Angina with Normal Coronaries, and Peripartum Cardiomyopathy
units.guide:
DCMP ECG shows small-voltage limb-lead complexes (high voltage chest leads), sinus tachycardia and poor R-wave progression; ECHO shows cardiomegaly, a large roomy thin-walled LV with raised end-diastolic dimensions/reduced EF and global hypokinesia (p333). MRI/angiogram rule out CAD in all, especially first presentation after age 30.
Angina with normal coronaries is boxed as myocarditis, HCM or Takotsubo CMP; treatment is transplant. Peripartum CMP has the best DCMP prognosis but high recurrence, is associated with pregnancy age >30 and hypertension, and presents postpartum or in the third trimester.
Its pathology is SFLT1 (soluble fibrin-like tyrosine kinase I, anti-angiogenic); LV systolic failure, dyspnea with minimal exertion/breastfeeding and diaphoresis appear, with advice to avoid pregnancy again and expected resolution in 3–4 months.

units.title: Drug-Induced Cardiomyopathy and Anthracycline Regimens, Alcohol-Induced Disease, and Myocarditis Onset and Etiology
units.sec: Drug-Induced Cardiomyopathy and Anthracycline Regimens, Alcohol-Induced Disease, and Myocarditis Onset and Etiology
units.guide:
Drug-induced CMP includes anthracyclines (doxorubicin, daunorubicin, mitoxantrone), trastuzumab, cyclophosphamide, VEGF inhibitors, proteasome inhibitors, anabolic steroids, lead, mercury, hydrocarbons and cocaine (p334). Anthracycline regimens noted are hydroxydaunorubicin in R-CHOP for NHL, Adriamycin/doxorubicin in ABVD for Hodgkin lymphoma and 7 + 3 for AML.
Alcohol-induced disease follows ACE polymorphism → acetaldehyde; added risks are holiday-heart AF, stroke and ACS, aggravated by thiamine/magnesium/selenium deficiency. Avoiding alcohol can improve EF after 3–6 months.
Myocarditis is focal or diffuse inflammatory dilated CMP, acute more than chronic (3 months), from post-viral HHV-6 (m/c) or Trypanosoma cruzi (Chaga's disease as printed), acting through systemic infection → severe cytokine release → reduced LV function.

units.title: The Clinical Spectrum of Myocarditis, ECG, Blood, HPE and MRI Findings, and Supportive Treatment
units.sec: The Clinical Spectrum of Myocarditis, ECG, Blood, HPE and MRI Findings, and Supportive Treatment
units.guide:
Most myocarditis is subclinical (p335). Unexplained tachycardia/hypotension after febrile infection can present with chest pain/angina despite normal coronaries or exertional dyspnea; refractory hypotension in infection and new-onset HF are poor-prognosis markers, while giant-cell myocarditis with rapidly progressive HF is linked to sarcoidosis.
ECHO shows global/LV dysfunction, ECG non-specific ST/T changes with low-voltage QRS and sinus tachycardia, blood shows troponin I elevation, HPE uses Dallas criteria and the MRI caption marks peripheral enhancement.
Treatment is no specific therapy, supportive care and steroids only for autoimmune disease.
